original.target_description: Experiment 5 Family Feud: scarcity-by-preview interaction in standardized performance; preview benefit differs between poor and rich.

n.exclusions: No additional exclusions reported for this test in the main article; complete 2×2 test corresponds to the stated 137 participants.
n.quote:
One hundred thirty-seven participants played
Family Feud.

replication.target_description: Experiment 5: corresponding scarcity-by-preview interaction in standardized performance.

n.exclusions: 41 of 1013 excluded for missing subject IDs, practice data saved in main file, or incorrect time allotment (>5 s deviation).
n.quote:
Forty-one participants were
excluded, leaving 972 for the analyses.

reported_success.location: p. 6, section 3.3; p. 5, Table 1, Experiment 5 Summary
reported_success.quote:
The findings from the replication
of Experiment 5 are in the same direction as in the original paper, but they are not significant and are much weaker.

notes: Matched primary interaction rather than rich-only or poor-only simple effects first reported in 2019. Both papers label this a scarcity × borrowing interaction in the printed result, although the manipulated second factor in Experiment 5 is previews. Original precision retained; 2019 restatement reports more precise original values. Narrative verdict classified mixed for same-direction but much-weaker result; authors say further testing is needed.
